title: Cell Mito Stress Test for Monocyte Mitochondrial Function
author: Brandt D Pence
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kw7cxhn
materials: Aspirate Cell-Tak solution if not already done.

Materials to Prepare: Seahorse DMEM Media : Add 50 μl pyruvate, 50 μl L-glutamine, 20 μl glucose to 5 ml Seahorse Base Medium. Sterile filter before use. Cell-Tak coated XFp plate. Prepare Cell-Tak. Add Cell-Tak and sodium hydroxide to 0.1 M sodium bicarbonate so that each well will receive 0.56 μg Cell-Tak, and sodium hydroxide concentration will be 0.63 mM. Cell-Tak concentration varies by batch, so calculations for each new batch will need to be performed. Add 25 μl Cell-Tak solution to each well. Plates can be stored at room temperature (at least 20 minutes) until use (for a few hours). Plates can also be prepped prior to assay day by incubating plates in Cell-Tak (at least 20 minutes), then aspirating remaining solution, air drying, and storing at 4degC until use. Monocytes Monocytes should be prepared as directed in the monocyte isolation protocol (https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kwtcxen). Isolated monocytes should be diluted to a concentration of 3×10^6 cells / ml in prepared Seahorse DMEM media prior to use in the assay. Use monocytes immediately.

steps.title: Hydrate sensor cartridge (day before)
steps.instruction: Turn on the Seahorse XFp analyzer overnight to warm up. Hydrate the XFp sensor cartridge by adding 200 µl XF calibration solution to each well of the cartridge and 400 µl sterile PBS or sterile water to each moat. Incubate the cartridge overnight at 37 °C in a non‑CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Seed cells and medium
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl assay medium to wells A and H of the utility plate and add 50 µl cell suspension (1.5 × 10⁵ cells per well) to wells B–G. Run samples in duplicate or triplicate as desired.

steps.title: Centrifuge seeded plate
steps.instruction: Place the utility plate in its carrier and centrifuge at 300 × g for 1 minute without brake.

steps.title: Add assay medium
steps.instruction: Add 130 µl assay medium to each well A–H, bringing the total volume in each well to 180 µl.

steps.title: Incubate plate 1 hour
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at 37 °C in a non‑CO₂ incubator for 1 hour.

steps.title: Prepare drug dilutions
steps.instruction: While the plate is incubating, prepare both preliminary and final drug dilutions as described.

substeps.instruction:
Preliminary dilutions (mix by pipetting up‑and‑down):
- 50 µM oligomycin (blue cap): add 252 µl medium.
- 50 µM FCCP (yellow cap): add 288 µl medium.
- 25 µM rotenone/antimycin A (red cap): add 216 µl medium.

Final dilutions:
- 10 µM oligomycin: mix 120 µl of the 50 µM oligomycin stock with 480 µl medium.
- 20 µM FCCP: mix 120 µl of the 50 µM FCCP stock with 180 µl medium.
- 5 µM rotenone/antimycin A: mix 60 µl of the 25 µM rotenone/antimycin A stock with 240 µl medium.

steps.title: Clear sensor bubbles
steps.instruction: Remove the sensor cartridge from the incubator, then briefly remove and re‑insert the sensors to expel any trapped air bubbles.

steps.title: Load injection ports
steps.instruction: Load the prepared drug solutions into the cartridge ports for the Cell Mito Stress Test:

substeps.instruction: Port A (all wells): 20 µl oligomycin → final 1 µM.

Port B (all wells): 22 µl oligomycin → final 2 µM (used for the second oligomycin injection; if only one injection is desired, prepare oligomycin so the final concentration after the first injection is 2 µM).
Port C (all wells): 25 µl FCCP → final 2 µM.
Port D (all wells): 27 µl rotenone/antimycin A → final 0.5 µM.

steps.title: Select program and calibrate
steps.instruction: On the Seahorse XFp software, select the Cell Mito Stress Test program (note that a custom program is required if two oligomycin injections are used). Calibrate the sensor cartridge by removing its lid as instructed by the software.

steps.title: Insert cell plate into XFp
steps.instruction: After the 1‑hour incubation, remove the utility plate from the XFp instrument and replace it with the cell plate (remove the plate lid before insertion).

steps.title: Run Cell Mito Stress Test
steps.instruction: Execute the Cell Mito Stress Test. Acquire three measurements per injection (including the basal measurement), which is sufficient for analysis.

steps.title: Image or collect protein
steps.instruction: When the run is finished, either photograph each well by photomicroscopy or lyse the wells and isolate protein to later normalize OCR values to cell number.

steps.title: Analyze OCR data
steps.instruction:
Calculate the following parameters for each condition (averages or mean/max may be used):
- Basal Respiration = (unstimulated OCR) – (rotenone/antimycin A OCR)
- ATP‑Linked Respiration = (unstimulated OCR) – (oligomycin OCR)
- Maximal Respiration = (FCCP OCR) – (rotenone/antimycin A OCR)
- Spare Capacity = (FCCP OCR) – (unstimulated OCR)
- Proton Leak = (oligomycin OCR) – (rotenone/antimycin A OCR)
- Non‑Mitochondrial Respiration = (rotenone/antimycin A OCR).
Refer to Figure 1 for a schematic of these calculations.
